findings.description: Every run started by a PR or review event sees its own `status` check run as `in_progress` on the PR head, so it labels `pr/ci-pending`. Several of those events never get a later recompute, so the label sticks.
findings.body:
**Every run started by a PR or review event labels the PR `pr/ci-pending`, and for several events nothing corrects it later.** ([pr-status.yml#L77-L83](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/89055ad1bb046cc64731fa7f8c61a36de2eaeba5/.github/workflows/pr-status.yml#L77-L83))

Runs started by `pull_request_target` and `pull_request_review` put their check run on the PR head commit. So `checks.listForRef({ ref: pr.head.sha })` returns this job's own `status` run while it is still `in_progress`, and

```js
if (data.check_runs.some((c) => c.status !== "completed")) return "pr/ci-pending";
```

returns `pr/ci-pending` unless an earlier branch matched first. Only `workflow_run` of "Claude Code Review" and `push` to `main` put their check runs on the default-branch commit, so only those two can fix the label afterwards.

In these cases the label stays wrong until the next push to `main`:
- **Approving or dismissing a review on a green PR.** Claude Code Review doesn't trigger on reviews. The poster's own review is submitted with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which starts no workflows.
- **`reopened`.** `claude-code-review.yml` listens only for `opened`, `ready_for_review` and `synchronize`.
- **Fork PRs.** `workflow_run.pull_requests` is empty for runs from a fork, and the Claude job is skipped anyway because the actor isn't the owner.
- **A Claude run that skips quickly** (non-owner pusher). It can finish before this run, which can spend about 12 s polling `mergeable`. Whichever run finishes last sets the label.

Suggested fix: leave this job's own check run out of the pending test, for example by matching `context.runId` in `c.details_url` or skipping this job's check name. Also consider adding `"Label PRs"` and this workflow to `workflow_run.workflows`, or using a `check_suite: completed` trigger, so the label is recomputed once the sibling checks finish.

findings.description: If this job fails, it leaves a failed `status` check on the PR head. Every later recompute then counts that failure and labels the PR `pr/ci-failing`. Review events on fork PRs trigger this every time.

There is no concurrency control and the label update is read-modify-write. Two runs on the same PR can both remove the old label and each add their own, leaving two `pr/*` labels. Or one run's `removeLabel` gets a 404 and fails the job.

The script never checks `pr.state`, and there is no `closed` trigger. A Claude review that finishes after a merge (`workflow_run.pull_requests`), or a review on a closed PR, still writes a `pr/*` label, and merged PRs keep their last `pr/ready` label forever.

Only check runs are read, never the `claude-review` commit status the poster sets on the head. An `@claude review` retry runs on `main` (its check run is not on the PR head, and its `workflow_run.pull_requests` is empty), so a successful retry never clears `pr/ci-failing` left by the failed `synchronize` check, and a failed retry never moves the PR off `pr/ready`.

Any GitHub account can set `pr/changes-requested` on any open PR in this public repo by submitting a "Request changes" review, and the label stays until that same user approves. The loop counts every reviewer's latest state with no `author_association` filter. GitHub's own review decision only counts reviewers with write access. Restricting the count to `["OWNER","MEMBER","COLLABORATOR"].includes(r.author_association)` closes it.

A fork author controls which check runs exist on their head SHA, so on fork PRs `pr/ready` only means "no check the PR's own workflows produced has failed". `pull_request` runs the workflow files from the PR, so the author can rewrite or delete `claude-code-review.yml`. The call also reads only the first 100 check runs (no `github.paginate`), so a PR that adds more than 100 passing matrix jobs could push a real failure off the page. Consider paginating, and treat the label as a hint rather than a merge signal.
The comment says `mergeable_state` is null until GitHub computes it, but the loop polls `mergeable` (`if (pr.mergeable !== null) break;`). The comment names the wrong field.

The header says the label is "Recomputed on every event that can change the answer: ... a finished workflow run", but `workflow_run` is filtered to "Claude Code Review" only. Other checks finishing never trigger a recompute, so "every event" overclaims.

The priority order is written twice: in the header comment and in the order of the `statusOf` branches (`LABELS` order mirrors it but drives nothing). The literal `workflows: ["Claude Code Review"]` must match the `name:` in `claude-code-review.yml`, and renaming that workflow would silently stop CI-driven recomputes.

The loop that removes stale labels and then adds the wanted one nearly copies the one in `labeler.yml` (lines 42-49). That is two uses, so under AGENTS.md's "no abstraction until third use" rule it is fine to leave for now.

The `actions/github-script` step has no `name:`, but the steps in sibling workflows `labeler.yml` and `claude-code-review.yml` are all named (AGENTS.md core rule: match the patterns of similar files).
